title: Writing with capital letters and full stops
summary: Learn to use capital letters and full stops in Spanish sentences.
keyIdeas: Sentences begin with a capital letter.
Names such as Lucía, Chispa and Madrid begin with a capital letter.
The statements in these exercises end with a full stop.

basicKnowledge: D. Reflexión sobre la lengua y sus usos en el marco de propuestas la producción y comprensión de textos orales, escritos o multimodales

activities.prompt: The first letter of a sentence is always a capital letter.
activities.explanation: All sentences begin with a capital letter.

activities.prompt: Which mark ends the Spanish sentence «Hugo juega en el patio»?
activities.explanation: This sentence makes a statement and ends with a full stop.
activities.hint: It is a small dot at the end of the sentence.

activities.prompt: Sort these Spanish words by their first letter.
activities.explanation: People's names, such as Martina and Hugo, begin with a capital letter.

activities.prompt: Match each name to the reason it begins with a capital letter.
activities.explanation: The names of people, pets and cities begin with a capital letter.

activities.prompt: Find the Spanish sentence with a mistake.
activities.explanation: The sentence «la casa es grande.» starts with a lower-case l. It needs a capital L.
activities.hint: Look carefully at the first letter of each sentence.

activities.prompt: Put the Spanish words in order: who sleeps, then the action, then where.
activities.explanation: The sentence begins with a capital letter in «El» and ends with the word with a full stop: «aquí.».

activities.prompt: Wei wants to write a message in Spanish to his grandmother. Which sentence is written correctly?
activities.explanation: The sentence starts with a capital letter in «Te» and ends with a full stop.
activities.hint: Find the sentence that begins with a capital letter and ends with a full stop.

activities.prompt: Choose the missing mark at the end of Nerea's Spanish note.
activities.explanation: This complete statement needs a full stop at the end.
activities.hint: It is the punctuation mark that ends this sentence.
activities.sentence: Hoy comemos arroz en el comedor___

activities.prompt: Read the Spanish text carefully and answer the questions.
activities.explanation: Chispa is a name. All the sentences in this text end with a full stop.
activities.title: La tortuga de Adrián
activities.text: Adrián tiene una tortuga pequeña. Se llama Chispa. Chispa come hojas de lechuga verde en el jardín. Los dos juegan juntos por la tarde.

questions.prompt: Why does «Chispa» begin with a capital letter?
questions.explanation: Chispa is the name of Adrián's pet, so it begins with a capital letter.
options: Because it is a tasty food.
Because it is a very long word.
Because it is the turtle's name.

questions.prompt: Which mark is at the end of each sentence in the text?
questions.explanation: Each of the four sentences ends with a full stop.
